quote: Contradiction detection in text is a critical task in NLU, aimed at identifying inconsistencies or conflicting information within textual data.
Document-level Self-Contradiction Detection (DSCD) takes a multi-sentence document as input and predicts a binary label indicating whether any self-contradictions exist.

In this work, we address the challenge of Document-level Self-Contradiction Detection (DSCD), where Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting has shown significant response inconsistency due to incomplete or variable focus during inference. To tackle this issue, we propose a two-stage framework combining supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning.
outputs: The model generates binary judgments (yes/no) on whether a document contains self-contradictions and, in the Judge then Find task, also outputs a list of contradictory sentences as evidence.

We employ a model-based approach with customized judgment prompts for more rigorous self-contradiction verification. Given a modified document di, a set of model-generated contradictory statements S, and a rationale r explaining the contradiction, the verification process evaluates the validity of the contradiction. Verification is conducted by querying an LLM M, formalized as Verdict = M(di, S, r), where Verdict indicates whether a valid contradiction is detected.
